title.value: SatBird: Bird Species Distribution Modeling with Remote Sensing and Citizen Science Data
title.justification: The title accurately captures the content of the paper, which focuses on using remote sensing and citizen science data to model bird species distribution.
title.quote: We introduce a novel task for mapping bird species to their habitats by predicting species encounter rates from satellite images, and present SatBird.

extractions.description: This paper introduces SatBird, a dataset and model that use remote sensing and citizen science data to predict bird species distribution and encounter rates. It focuses on improving biodiversity monitoring by leveraging data from satellite images and citizen science observations to inform conservation policy planning. The task is to map bird species to their habitats and predict encounter rates using satellite images, emphasizing the model's application in biodiversity and ecosystem monitoring. The approach suggests the potential for scalable monitoring of ecosystems worldwide, particularly in areas with limited biodiversity data.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper discusses the impacts of climate change on biodiversity and the importance of understanding species distribution to inform policy decisions. It directly links its work to climate change by noting its major role in biodiversity loss, affecting ecosystem services and human wellbeing.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Climate change is a major driver of biodiversity loss, affecting ecosystem services which, in turn, impacts various human wellbeing aspects.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on biodiversity monitoring and protection by using remote sensing to model bird species distribution, which directly aligns with the Natural Systems Protection category.
primary_category.quote: We introduce a novel task for mapping bird species to their habitats by predicting species encounter rates from satellite images.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper involves using climate data alongside satellite imagery to understand habitat switches and species distribution, which ties into climate modeling and predictions.
secondary_categories.quote: We use bird sighting records from the citizen science database eBird, which has 80 million records of almost all 10000 global bird species.

primary_sub_category.justification: The task of the paper revolves around predicting bird species encounter rates and understanding species distribution, which is directly related to the biodiversity sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our contributions include: Proposing and framing the task of predicting bird species encounter rates jointly at a specific location using remote sensing data.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper supports its ecosystem monitoring and species distribution by incorporating climate datasets and discussing their importance in understanding shifts due to climate change.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: It is crucial to understand the changing distributions of species globally to inform policy decisions, for example in shaping land use and land conservation choices.

applications.value: Predicting bird species encounter rates for biodiversity monitoring.
applications.justification: This application is central to the paper's goals, as it aims to improve our understanding of biodiversity distribution through predictive modeling.
applications.quote: Our contributions include: Proposing and framing the task of predicting bird species encounter rates jointly at a specific location using remote sensing data.
